content: Do not judge the courage of a captain while the ship is tied securely to the wooden pier.
author: Celtic & Norse Proverbs
explanation: When docked in harbor, any amateur can wear an officer's jacket and bark orders with a confident smirk. Only when the ship clears the headlands, the swells rise thirty feet, and the rigging screams in the dark do you discover who has the stomach to lead. Character requires the deep water.
practicalInsight: Do not boast of your strength until you have stood firm in the deep water of real adversity.
reflectionPrompt: Are you testing your courage in real deep waters, or remaining in the safe harbor where anyone can pose as a captain?
